An earlier generation reported a 0-30 business day review, citing a real sentence — 'you have 30 days to make those changes' — which is the developer's deadline to respond to a quality check, not Shopify's review time. It had also absorbed Built for Shopify badge requirements (50 net installs, five reviews, a minimum rating), which belong to a recognition programme and not to registering an OAuth app. Both errors shared one cause: conflating getting credentials with getting listed. Shopify's docs state the client ID and secret are available immediately, and that distribution is a separate later choice where custom distribution needs no review at all. After the fix the guide reports the review wait as unknown with the right reasoning, and the summary correctly says credentials are issued instantly. Two things remain wrong: the tier is pushed to Days by a quality-check response step that only applies if you pursue public distribution, and the guide says 'Partner Dashboard' where Shopify's current docs say 'Dev Dashboard' at dev.shopify.com/dashboard. steps.title: Log in with a qualified user
steps.detail: Sign into the Xero Developer Portal using a user that has Standard, Adviser, or Administrator level permissions and the Connected Apps permission.

citations.quote: The user that connects the integration has to have either Standard, Adviser, or Administrator level user with the Connected Apps permission.

steps.title: Navigate to My Apps
steps.detail: From the dashboard, click the “My Apps” menu item to view existing apps and create a new one.

steps.title: Create a new app
steps.detail: Press the “Add App” (or “Create New App”) button and provide the required name, description, and company details.
steps.where: Developer Portal > My Apps > Add App

steps.title: Add Partner Login URL
steps.detail: Enter a Partner Login URL in the “Partner Login URL” field. Leaving it blank will prevent the app from appearing in the Xero Partner Hub App Launcher.
steps.where: Developer Portal > My Apps > App Settings

citations.quote: Add your Partner Login URL , using the same pattern as your existing Login URL.
Leave it blank: Your app won’t appear in the launcher, regardless of how well it works elsewhere for individual organisations.

steps.title: Register redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add up to 50 exact redirect URIs (wildcards are not supported). Each URI must match the one used in the OAuth flow.
steps.where: Developer Portal > My Apps > App Settings > Redirect URIs

citations.quote: You can use up to 50 redirect URIs for your app.
The use of wildcards in redirect URI is not supported.

steps.title: Select scopes
steps.detail: For apps created on or after 2 March 2026, choose granular scopes (available from April 2026). For older apps, you may continue using broad scopes but must migrate before September 2027 if you need granular access.
steps.where: Developer Portal > My Apps > App Settings > Scopes

citations.quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 will use the new granular scopes
They’ll be available for you to request from April 2026
Apps created before 2 March 2026 will have until September 2027 to move from broad scopes to granular scopes

steps.title: Save and activate the app
steps.detail: Click the “Save” or “Create App” button. The app becomes active immediately; no additional review wait is required.

nuances.title: Partner Login URL must not be empty
nuances.detail: If the Partner Login URL field is left blank, the app will not appear in the Xero Partner Hub App Launcher, even if all other settings are correct.

citations.quote: Leave it blank: Your app won’t appear in the launcher, regardless of how well it works elsewhere for individual organisations.

nuances.title: Redirect URI wildcards unsupported
nuances.detail: Only exact URIs are accepted; using ‘*’ or pattern matching will cause validation errors.

citations.quote: The use of wildcards in redirect URI is not supported.

nuances.title: Single‑page applications not supported
nuances.detail: Xero OAuth 2.0 does not currently support SPA flows; use a server‑side or native app pattern instead.

citations.quote: Single page apps are not currently supported.

nuances.title: Granular scopes not retroactive
nuances.detail: Existing tokens for apps created before 2 March 2026 retain their original (broad) scopes. Granular scopes only apply after the user re‑authorises with the updated scope list.

citations.quote: The granular scopes won’t automatically be applied to any existing tokens. So, the granular scope won’t be applied to any new authorisations until they are added to the authorisation link your customers are using and the customer reauthorises your app

nuances.title: 401 error for missing granular scope
nuances.detail: Calling an endpoint that requires a granular scope you haven’t requested returns a 401 Forbidden with header WWW-Authenticate:insufficient_scope.

citations.quote: The API will return a 401 forbidden error with a response header WWW-Authenticate:insufficent_scope

nuances.title: Access token lifetime
nuances.detail: Access tokens are valid for 30 minutes; plan token refresh accordingly.

nuances.title: Refresh token expiration
nuances.detail: Refresh tokens that are not used for 60 days expire and require the user to re‑authorise the app.

citations.quote: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days. If you don’t refresh your access token within 60 days the user will need to reauthorise your app.

nuances.title: PKCE support for native apps
nuances.detail: Native applications can use the PKCE extension and omit a client secret, improving security.

citations.quote: Xero supports the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension to the authorization code flow. This allows native apps to securely connect to our API without needing to store a client secret.

whenBlocked.situation: Current user lacks Standard/Adviser/Administrator level with Connected Apps permission
